articleBody:
Preparing for a kitchen addition requires gathering key details before you commit to construction. Use this checklist to keep your project organized and ensure your contractor has clear guidance on your expectations.

- [ ] Property boundary and zoning confirmation — Verifies that extending your kitchen footprint complies with local setback rules.
- [ ] Identification of load-bearing walls — Determines whether structural beams and engineering drawings are required for open layouts.
- [ ] Dedicated electrical circuit map — Ensures heavy kitchen appliances, microwaves, and islands receive adequate panel capacity.
- [ ] Plumbing drain and vent line routing — Confirms adequate fall and venting for relocated sinks, dishwashers, and ice makers.
- [ ] Confirmed cabinet order with field dimensions — Prevents costly misfits between framed openings and manufactured box sizes.
- [ ] Mechanical exhaust pathway — Plans an exterior duct route for your range hood instead of recirculating fumes.
- [ ] Written allowance schedule for finishes — Clarifies budgeted amounts for tile, countertops, fixtures, and cabinet hardware.
- [ ] Subcontractor trade management plan — Identifies who oversees plumbing, electrical, and mechanical trades on site.

How to use this checklist:
Review each item with your general contractor during the initial walk-through. Nailing down these technical requirements early prevents mid-project change orders. Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC acts as your lead contact, coordinating trade partners while delivering hands-on finish carpentry, drywall, and tile work. Call 303-505-0866 to review your kitchen addition checklist.
